name: Afghan Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Sign language; only known linguistic work is Power 2014 MA thesis on handshapes — nothing describing (spoken-style) word stress; category inapplicable.

sources.citation: UND Scholarly Commons landing page for Power 2014 (https://commons.und.edu/theses/1695/) — abstract, advisor Kathryn L. Hansen, committee J. Albert Bickford, Adam Baker.
Power, Justin. 2014. Handshapes in Afghan Sign Language. MA thesis, University of North Dakota (Theses and Dissertations 1695), xv+101 pp. (117-page PDF).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a university library login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing. The whole thesis is a feature analysis of the handshape parameter (selected fingers, thumb configuration, arrangement, aperture) in 300+ signs from seven Deaf male signers; 'prosodic' occurs only in the survey of Brentari's Prosodic Model for ASL (ch. 2); no mention of stress, accent, rhythm, emphasis or nonmanuals for AFSL; p. 94 (PDF 110) lists movement and location contrast as future research. Text layer uses a shifted font encoding (decoded copy).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Afghan Sign Language' (refs: Power 2023 'Tajik Sign Language in Context' in Ido & Mahmoodi-Bakhtiari eds, Tajik Linguistics, De Gruyter; Brown 2012 ReliefWeb; Power 2006 ISO request; Ethnologue 25).
sources.note: History and distribution only; no linguistic description.

sources.citation: Afghan National Association of the Deaf et al. 1387 [2008]. Farhang-e zaban-e eshara-ye Afghani = Afghan Sign Language Dictionary. Kabul. (ACKU digital repository, DOI 10.29171/acku_hv2476_5_alif77_fay4_1387)
sources.note: Opened only: 149 MB image-only scan whose text layer is just the ACKU watermark (checked pp. 1-15); not scanned because it is a sign dictionary (Dari/Pashto/English glosses) with no prose on prosody to be expected. Nothing on stress seen.

sources.citation: Power, Justin. 2006. ISO 639-3 Change Request 2006-041 (create afg, Afghan Sign Language) + Request for New Language Code Element + CR comments (Bickford 2007). SIL ISO 639-3 Registration Authority.
sources.note: Nothing on structure; sociolinguistic and historical notes only. Lists the SHIP/CDAP/HIFA 2000 dictionary 'A Collection of Signs' (c. 2000 signs) with 'a very basic and brief explanation of sign language grammar in the introduction' as the only published source.

sources.citation: Power, Justin M. 2023. Tajik Sign Language in Context. In Shinji Ido & Behrooz Mahmoodi-Bakhtiari (eds), Tajik Linguistics. Berlin: De Gruyter. ISBN 978-3-11-061953-9.

sources.note: Most recent academic treatment mentioning AFSL (as distinct from Tajik SL); by the only linguist who has worked on AFSL; would supersede nothing on stress but is the newest primary-adjacent source.

sources.citation: Serve's Hearing Impaired Project, Hearing Impaired Foundation of Afghanistan & Comprehensive Disabled Afghans Program. 2000. Afghan Sign Language [A Collection of Signs]. Kabul: CDAP (UN). c. 2000 signs.
